headline: Apple limits iPhone Duo orders to two per customer to curb scalping
summary: Apple is implementing a strict purchase limit on its new iPhone Duo devices in an effort to combat scalpers and ensure wider availability for genuine customers.
details: Apple has announced a new policy limiting customers to a maximum of two iPhone Duo units per purchase. This measure is being rolled out across major markets, including the US and UK.
The company aims to prevent resellers and scalpers from buying up large quantities of the new device, which often leads to inflated prices on the secondary market.
This move comes as demand for new Apple products frequently outstrips supply, creating opportunities for those looking to profit from scarcity.
By enforcing this limit, Apple hopes to make the iPhone Duo more accessible to its intended customer base and maintain a fairer purchasing experience.

topic: google home speakers download hundreds of gigabytes of data
headline_marked: [[Google Home speakers]] downloading hundreds of GBs of data daily
headline: Google Home speakers downloading hundreds of GBs of data daily
summary: A bug is causing some Google Home smart speakers to repeatedly download updates, potentially leading to massive data overages for users with limited internet plans.
details: Users have reported that their Google Home smart speakers are downloading hundreds of gigabytes of data per day. This issue is not easily noticeable unless users check their router settings for device-specific data usage.

The problem appears to stem from a stuck update process that causes the speaker to re-download software multiple times a day. While some users have reported massive numbers like 200GB in a single day, others have seen smaller but still significant amounts like 35GB daily.

While older models of Google Home speakers seem unaffected, anecdotal evidence suggests newer devices might be more susceptible to this bug. Users are advised to check their internet logs to monitor their speaker's data consumption.

If a Google Home speaker is found to be consuming excessive data, the recommended temporary solution is to unplug the device. Google has confirmed it is aware of the issue and is actively working on a fix to resolve the data drain problem.
